ogis — agent notes

Source: AGENTS.md

Seeded 2026-11-18 by Claude (AI), from ogis’s code, NEWS and git log, its Claude memories and fishycode’s records; not yet read by the maintainer. What is true now: keep it short and current, and change it in the same commit as the fact it records.

What ogis is

Interactive maps for marine data, drawn in the browser by MapLibre GL JS. The data stay in DuckDB and reach the page as vector tiles, so a map of millions of rows stays fast. A map is served from R on the local machine (og_serve()) or written as a folder that opens from its index.html with no R (og_bundle()). It is a general package, in the company of leaflet, mapview and tmap: generic, not Icelandic, not for fishing alone.

There are three doors to a map (fishycode plan 072):

  • the layer functions in the pipe, named after ggplot2’s geoms (og_map() |> og_point() |> og_path());
  • a layer in MapLibre’s own terms (og_layer(), og_add_layer());
  • one-line maps of a known kind (og_tracks(), og_cells(), og_names(), og_relief(), og_contour()).

og_view() is still to come. ogis began as ramb’s map viewer (rb_map*()). It moved out as rebelrebel (rr_) on 2026-11-10 and was renamed ogis (og_) on 2026-11-18 (fishycode decision 327). Older NEWS entries and fishycode’s plans keep the names of their day.

Where things are

Path Holds
R/map.R og_map(), og_section(), og_layer(), the page’s config. .og_map_engine (now 7) must equal ENGINE in the page; change both together whenever the page and the server stop fitting each other.
R/serve.R og_serve(), og_stop(), the server (.og_map_app()): /config.json, /meta, /time, /fit, /row, /search, /data, /tiles, /notes, /verdicts, and a map’s own routes under /x/. .og_map_query() reads every query the way a form writes it (+ is a space).
R/layers.R The layer functions: og_point(), og_path(), og_line(), og_segment(), og_polygon(), og_text().
R/time.R, R/tracks.R og_time(), the time panel under the map; og_tracks(), vessel tracks in one line.
R/cells.R, R/names.R, R/relief.R og_cells(), og_names(), og_relief(), og_contour().
R/tiles.R, R/pmtiles.R, R/bundle.R Tile makers (og_tiles_table(), og_tiles_dem(), og_tiles_mbtiles()), the PMTiles writer, og_bundle().
R/notes.R, R/script.R, R/quick.R Readers’ notes and verdicts; og_script(), a page’s own script; og_add_layer().
R/colours.R, R/palettes.R, R/duckdb.R, R/example.R Colours, palettes and base maps; DuckDB connections; og_example().
inst/engine/index.html The page: one file (~2,950 lines) of HTML, CSS and JavaScript, served and bundled alike.
inst/engine/vendor/ MapLibre GL JS 6.19.0 repackaged as classic scripts, pmtiles.js, maplibre-contour and uPlot, each with its licence (inst/COPYRIGHTS).
inst/extdata/ The example parquet files, stored with Git LFS (og_example()).
tests/testthat/ Tests. Helpers: helper-browser.R (headless Chrome through chromote: open_page(), page_eval(), wait_until(), serve_dir()), helper-spatial.R (skip_if_no_spatial(), mvt_count()), helper-pmtiles.R.
vignettes/articles/ Quarto articles with live maps (ogis, labels, own-page, tracks), built into the pkgdown site.
tools/ Run by hand at each MapLibre update: vendor-maplibre.R <version>, then firefox-check.R.
data-raw/ How the example files were changed.
.github/workflows/ R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu; the pkgdown site, rebuilt on every push to main.

How a change lands

  1. Work in a worktree on a branch (git worktree add) when another session may be using ~/R/Pakkar/ogis: one may hold uncommitted work there, or serve maps from it. Never switch that checkout’s branch.
  2. A test that fails before the change and passes after it. A change to the page also gets a headless-Chrome test: served (og_serve(wait = FALSE) and open_page()), or bundled (og_bundle() and serve_dir()).
  3. Bump the version in DESCRIPTION with each change: YYYY.MM.DD for the day’s first, then .1, .2.
  4. Add a NEWS.md entry under a heading # ogis <version> at the top: bullets with a bold lead, what changed and why, the maintainer’s words where the choice was theirs, and measured numbers.
  5. Run R under LANG=en_US.UTF-8 LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8. R in Claude’s shell does not start in UTF-8. There, devtools::document() writes <U+00F6> into other Rd files (revert those), and eight notes and verdicts tests skip.
  6. Check: devtools::test(). It sets NOT_CRAN; without it the Chrome tests skip. Two tests run only against the installed ogis: a Quarto document’s maps, and og_serve(wait = TRUE) from Rscript. Then devtools::check(), and pkgdown::build_article() for an article. The change is done when CI passes on all three systems.
  7. Commit message: what changed, with the version in brackets, e.g. og_cells() and og_names(): ... (2026.11.18.15). Commit as work lands; push only when asked, since each push to main rebuilds the public site.
  8. Install from a clone with LFS: remotes::install_git("https://github.com/einarhjorleifsson/ogis", git = "external", force = TRUE). install_github() installs the LFS pointers instead of the data, and over such an install, from the same commit, remotes skips without force = TRUE. packageDescription("ogis") says what is installed; RemoteSha is empty after an install from the local tree.

Rules

  • The repository and the site are public. Never put Icelandic internal data into the package, its tests, articles or site: the depth model, the effort cells, the place names, vessel data, or anything made from them. Each of these reaches ogis as one file, named by OGIS_DEPTH, OGIS_CELLS or OGIS_NAMES in .Renviron. Articles use public data: og_example() (ramb’s dansk, the 2019 March survey), EMODnet, GEBCO.
  • Platform independent (the maintainer, 2026-11-17): Linux, macOS and Windows alike. Use file.path() and tempfile(), never /tmp or a shell call. Write files as UTF-8 explicitly. Tests that need Chrome skip where there is none.
  • Articles are the feedback loop (2026-11-17): each feature lands with an article that builds a real map with it. Code that is long or awkward in an article, or needs :::, means the functions are wrong.
  • ogis does not depend on ramb. ramb is installed only for the site’s tracks article (Config/Needs/website).
  • ogis views; it does not edit (2026-11-17, fishycode plan 076). A page that edits builds on ogis’s documented surface: og_script(), og_serve(routes = ), and in the page og.on(), og.state(), og.fetch(), og.window(). It uses no ::: and no copied page. A fault such a page finds is fixed in ogis, with a test.
  • Keep it simple (2026-11-11): options studied and set aside are not built unasked. These include MLT, GeoArrow with deck.gl, DuckDB-WASM, FlatGeobuf, and a .duckdb file as the store (parquet stays the store).
  • MapLibre is pinned. It changes only at a chosen version, through tools/vendor-maplibre.R, checked in Chrome (the suite), Firefox (tools/firefox-check.R) and Safari (fishycode plan 077, decision 328).

Records

ogis keeps no plans or decisions of its own. NEWS.md says what changed, and fishycode (~/stasi/fishycode) holds the designs and choices:

  • plans: 072 (the package), 076 (a foundation for pages built on it), 077 (MapLibre 6);
  • decisions: 327 (the rename), 328 (MapLibre 6.19), 329 (the Icelandic example data for ramb and ogis);
  • TODO item 198;
  • from ramb’s map viewer: decisions 220, 228 and 277-281, and plans 046, 063 and 064.

The studies are under $FISHYDATA/archive/ (2026-11-11-rebelrebel-* and others).
